proposed_from.topic: Derive the exact 2^K-response-type minimax game for fixed K>=3 binary-potential-outcome contrasts under unrestricted designs and estimators. Prove C0=(sum_a |c_a|)^2/4 and determine the second-order exponent. Establish the universal Theta(n^(-4/3)) improvement using an explicit contrast-weighted clipped-shrinkage rule and an unrestricted embedded two-arm converse; give exact-rational finite-program procedure/prior certificates for rational contrasts and continuity-transfer certificates for every real contrast. Characterize the remaining sharp frontier—convergence, exact constant or subsequential set, second-order optimality of q*, optimizer/prior convergence, and any face/corner HJB, spectral, separable, or other limiting operator—as explicit unresolved questions. Include the K=3 c=(1,-1/2,-1/2) n<=5 showcase and ACTG 175 consumer.

seed_details.one_line: Exact orbit game for unrestricted fixed-\(K\) binary contrasts, reducing nature to \(2^K\) response-type counts and the statistician to allocation and observed-success orbits.
seed_details.anchor_locator: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026), Theorems 1--2 and the proof of Theorem 2; Hull (2026), Theorem 1, proof Steps 1--3, and Section 4.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The two-arm coordinatewise swap group makes the transformed assignment ancillary; a fixed \(K\)-arm coefficient vector is not preserved by a transitive arm-swap group, so one must retain the allocation and response-type orbit likelihood.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from unit symmetrization, because every finite experiment can be quotiented by relabeling units.
seed_details.rebuttal: Symmetrization alone does not supply the explicit hypergeometric orbit likelihood, the lossless joint design--estimator convex game, or a saddle point useful for a converse and asymptotics; those are the theorem-level objects.
seed_details.status: survived and chosen as the finite foundation

seed_details.one_line: Contrast-weighted first-order saddle point with \(q_a^\star\propto |c_a|\) and \(C_0=(\sum_a|c_a|)^2/4\), valid against every randomized design and estimator.
seed_details.anchor_locator: Hull (2026), Proposition 1 and Theorem 1; Bai (2023), Theorems 2.1, 3.1, and 3.2.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The affine upper bound becomes the allocation-simplex program \(\min_q\sum_a c_a^2/(4q_a)\), while the unrestricted lower bound requires a least-favorable response-type prior that defeats biased estimators and every design.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from Neyman allocation, because minimizing \(\sum_a c_a^2/q_a\) gives \(q_a\propto |c_a|\).
seed_details.rebuttal: That calculation proves only an upper bound for a named centered estimator; the new content is equality for the unrestricted design--estimator game and a design-uniform converse.
seed_details.status: survived and integrated into the chosen angle

seed_details.one_line: Second-order simplex collision frontier that determines the normalization, constant, and whether the continuum limit is a face/corner HJB, an elliptic cone operator, or a scalar separation.
seed_details.anchor_locator: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026), Theorem 3, Section 3 heuristic, and Section 6 upper and lower bounds; Levit (1986), principal Schrödinger-operator characterization.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Scalar localization by \(|\theta|\) must be replaced by an active-face stratification of response-type and allocation simplices before a Stein expansion or prior-information inequality can select the scale.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from the two-arm Airy proof after replacing one derivative by a gradient.
seed_details.rebuttal: Simultaneous faces create anisotropic diffusion, corner compatibility conditions, and possibly separability or a different balance; none is determined by a formal gradient substitution.
seed_details.status: survived as the principal open frontier

seed_details.one_line: Exact-rational \(K=3\), \(c=(1,-1/2,-1/2)\) grid-action LP hierarchy with a certified approximation error small enough to diagnose the second-order scale.
seed_details.anchor_locator: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026), Appendix A finite convex program and Section 3 numerical scaling plot.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The scalar endpoint rule indexed by one binomial count becomes a joint design--estimator orbit program indexed by three allocation counts, three observed success counts, and eight response-type counts.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is only computation and the exact squared-loss problem is not an LP.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection is correct for the continuous-action game; the retained object is a rational grid-action LP hierarchy with a proved bracket to the exact convex game, used as a falsification device rather than the paper's headline.

seed_details.one_line: Contrast-symmetry criterion characterizing when arm-randomization averaging makes the allocation ancillary, and when the two-arm reduction is impossible.
seed_details.anchor_locator: Hull (2026), proof of Theorem 1, Step 1; Bai (2023), Theorem 2.1 and Remark 2.2.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the binary XOR Haar average by the stabilizer of the signed coefficient vector and determine whether its orbits support a design-independent transformed experiment.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is a routine representation-theory restatement of invariance.
seed_details.rebuttal: The necessity direction must construct two response schedules with the same proposed quotient but different design information, which directly determines when an unrestricted minimax reduction exists.
seed_details.status: supporting route, not a separate headline

seed_details.one_line: Vector-contrast matrix-loss response-type game deciding when cross-arm minimax shrinkage strictly dominates coordinatewise scalar shrinkage.
seed_details.anchor_locator: Rosenman and Hunter (2026), Sections 2--4 and Gaussian quadratic-form risk calculations; Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026), Theorems 1--3.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The Gaussian SURE identity must be replaced by the exact assignment likelihood conditional on \(2^K\) response-type counts and a matrix-loss least-favorable prior valid against all designs.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from James--Stein shrinkage applied to the vector of difference-in-means estimators.
seed_details.rebuttal: Gaussian domination does not imply finite-population minimaxity, and shared arm outcomes make coordinatewise scalar games fail to compose under unrestricted designs.
seed_details.status: dropped from v1 because matrix loss changes the estimand and doubles the converse burden

seed_details.one_line: Weak-null randomization inference for a nonlinear multi-arm minimax rule, uniformly across active-face changes.
seed_details.anchor_locator: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026), Section 7 discussion; Wu and Ding (2021), studentized imputation construction and weak-null asymptotic validity theorem.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The finite-population linear representation must control nonlinear shrinkage bias and active-face switching uniformly on least-favorable local schedules.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from studentizing the shrinkage estimator and applying the multi-treatment finite-population central limit theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: The shrinkage correction is of the same order as the local least-favorable remainder and is nonregular at face switches, so ordinary linearization is not uniform.
seed_details.status: dropped until the estimator and its active-face geometry are known

seed_details.one_line: Bounded nonbinary multi-arm contrast game using endpoint priors and a multivariate Bernstein extension of the finite endpoint rule.
seed_details.anchor_locator: Hull (2026), Theorem 1 attainment by a separately convex Bernstein extension; Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026), bounded-outcome Theorem 2.3 and its Bernoulliization proof.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Separate convexity must be established jointly over \(K\) potential-outcome coordinates while the estimator observes only one coordinate and the contrast is not arm-exchangeable.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate by applying the two-arm endpoint reduction coordinate by coordinate.
seed_details.rebuttal: Coordinatewise extensions need not correspond to one common estimator or one common assignment law, and their risks interact through the scalar contrast.
seed_details.status: dropped because binary endpoint schedules already contain the hard converse

seed_details.one_line: Covariate-stratified unrestricted multi-arm minimaxity with contrast-weighted allocation inside prognostic strata.
seed_details.anchor_locator: Hull (2026), Section 4 conclusion on prognostic structure; Bai (2023), block-permutation Example 2.2 and Theorem 3.3.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The endpoint adversary must obey a within-stratum prognostic restriction, so the design-uniform prior cannot be formed by unconstrained independent endpoint signs.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate by solving the no-covariate game independently within each stratum.
seed_details.rebuttal: A global contrast and unrestricted estimator can borrow across strata, while the least-favorable law must certify that separate stratum games compose.
seed_details.status: dropped as a follow-on after the unstratified saddle point

proposed_from.literature_map: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026, Theorems 1--3 and the proofs in Sections 5--6) solve the unrestricted two-arm binary problem by a design-ancillary transformed experiment, a finite minimax saddle point, a nonlinear posterior-mean rule, and a scalar Airy boundary layer. Their design-uniform lower bound is the closest proof ancestor, but its treatment-swap construction has no transitive analogue for a fixed multi-arm contrast. Hull (2026, Theorem 1 and its three-step proof) independently obtains the same two-arm endpoint game by averaging over coordinatewise treatment swaps and extending the endpoint rule by separate convexity; the group-averaging step is the first step that changes when the contrast coefficients are not preserved by arm permutations. Bai (2023, Theorems 2.1 and 3.1--3.3) proves complete-randomization minimaxity under permutation-invariant superpopulation classes and derives Neyman allocation for linear estimators, but does not optimize over arbitrary biased estimators against fixed binary response schedules. Levit (1986) connects second-order minimax corrections to positive solutions and principal spectral quantities of problem-specific Schrödinger operators; this supplies an elliptic technique ancestor but does not resolve stratified simplex boundaries.
